<think>
Okay, I need to create a momentum-based trading strategy using the specified indicators: CCI, ATR, Stochastic, and Ichimoku. Let me think about how each of these can be used for entry and exit signals.

First, the entry rules. I want to capture momentum, so perhaps when the CCI crosses above a certain level, say 100, it indicates strong upward momentum. That could be a buy signal. For sell signals, when CCI drops below -100, it might indicate a strong downtrend.

Next, the Stochastic Oscillator. When the %K line crosses above %D and both are below 20, it's a bullish signal. Conversely, when %K crosses below %D and both are above 80, it's bearish. This helps confirm overbought or oversold conditions.

Ichimoku Cloud can help identify support and resistance. If the price is above the Kumo cloud, it's a bullish sign, and below it is bearish. Also, the Tenkan-sen and Kijun-sen lines: if Tenkan is above Kijun, it's bullish, and vice versa.

For exit rules, using ATR makes sense for volatility-based stops. ATR can help set dynamic stop-loss and take-profit levels. Maybe set stop-loss at 2x ATR below the entry price for longs and take-profit at 1x ATR above.

Risk management is important. Using time-based exits, like closing positions after 5 days, can prevent holding onto trades too long. Also, position sizing based on ATR and account size will help manage risk. For example, risking 2% of the account on each trade, calculating the position size based on ATR and stop-loss distance.

I should structure the strategy with these components: entry rules using CCI and Stochastic, exit rules with ATR and time-based exits, risk management with position sizing and stop-loss/take-profit levels. Now, I'll outline the code structure, initializing indicators, checking for signals each day, and executing trades with proper risk management.

entry_price.index >= self.max_hold_days:\n            return True\n\n        # Stop-loss and take-profit\n        if entry_type == 'long' and self.data['Low'][index] <= self.stop_loss:\n            return True\n        elif entry_type == 'short' and self.data['High'][index] >= self.stop_loss:\n            return True\n\n        if entry_type == 'long' and self.data['High'][index] >= self.take_profit:\n            return True\n        elif entry_type == 'short' and self.data['Low'][index] <= self.take_profit:\n            return True\n\n        return False\n\n    def execute_strategy(self):\n        signals = pd.DataFrame(index=self.data.index, columns=['position'])\n        signals['position'] = 0\n\n        for index in range(len(self.data)):\n            if index < 14:\n                continue  # Allow indicators to initialize\n\n            entry_type = self.check_entry(index)\n            if entry_type is not None:\n                signals.loc[self.data.index[index], 'position'] = 1 if entry_type == 'long' else -1\n                self.entry_price = self.data['Close'][index]\n                self.position_size = self.calculate_position_size()\n\n            if signals['position'][index] != 0:\n                if self.check_exit(index, entry_type, self.data.index[index]):\n                    signals.loc[self.data.index[index], 'position'] = 0\n\n        return signals\n```"
